body: Founder's original ask ('can we... connect from my phones minecraft, to debug') was only tested manually once earlier today. Made it real and persistent: new user-level systemd unit (dragonfly-debug.service) supervises the real df-mc/dragonfly fork (emilyspringerton/dragonfly, confirmed genuine earlier today -- zero commits ahead of upstream), auto-restarting on failure. Confirmed listening on UDP :19132 and logging real startup (mc-version=1.26.30) under supervision via ss -ulnp and the service's own log. Serves vanilla dragonfly content only, not GoblinFoxDragon's own Meadow biome -- that needs a separate, much larger world-provider integration sourcing from server/worldapi's ProceduralWorldStore, not attempted here. Honest, named gap: WAN/firewall reachability from a phone outside this box's own LAN was NOT verified -- no sudo access this session to check firewall/security-group rules for inbound UDP :19132, so same-LAN connectivity is confirmed but public reachability is not. The systemd unit is deployed locally only (~/.config/systemd/user/), not committed into ~/dragonfly itself -- that's the founder's own personal fork of a real external open-source project, and build binaries/service units don't belong in that repo's git history. GoblinFoxDragon 84de13f (docs/changelog only, since the service unit itself lives outside any git repo).
title: Real dragonfly fork deployed as persistent supervised service
